source_meta._title: Double-tapping forward button to sprint cannot be disabled/reconfigured

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 client, English-language user interface, keyboard and mouse, and a new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world. Creative mode is selected so the hunger requirement is not applicable. Use a clean game profile or game directory so Forward initially uses its default W binding and G is unused.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, the first affected version listed in the report; do not use the fixed version 25w31a.
Use an unmodified client without mods that alter movement, sprinting, key bindings, or input handling.
Use keyboard controls. Forward must initially be bound to W, and G must not be assigned to another action.
Create or enter a world where the player can move across a level, unobstructed stretch of ground.
Keep the player on the ground throughout the test; do not activate Creative flight.
Do not press the separately configured Sprint control, whose default input is Left Ctrl, during either double-tap sequence.
Do not crouch, collide with a block, open a GUI, or hold another movement control while performing a double-tap.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher using a clean vanilla installation configured for Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, then launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.15.2 main menu is displayed.

steps.action: From the main menu, open the controls screen by selecting Options and then Controls.
steps.success_cue: The Controls screen is open and the movement key bindings are visible or can be reached by scrolling.

steps.action: Locate the Forward movement binding. If it does not display W, click its binding button and press W. Leave it unchanged if it already displays W.
steps.success_cue: The Forward entry displays W as its assigned key.

steps.action: Confirm that G is not assigned to another control. With clean default 1.15.2 controls, G should be unused. Do not assign G yet.
steps.success_cue: Forward remains bound to W, and no other control is assigned to G.

steps.action: Return to the main menu by selecting Done on the Controls screen and then Done on the Options screen.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is displayed.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list and begin creating a new world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is displayed.

steps.action: Enter a recognizable world name and cycle the Game Mode button until it displays Creative.
steps.exact_input: World Name: MC-203401; Game Mode: Creative
steps.success_cue: The world name is set and the creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Open More World Options and cycle the World Type setting until Superflat is selected, then return to the primary world-creation screen.
steps.exact_input: More World Options... -> World Type: Superflat -> Done
steps.success_cue: The world is configured as a Creative-mode Superflat world.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for generation and loading to finish.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the world, nearby terrain is rendered, movement responds normally, and the player is not flying.

steps.action: Turn the player to face a level, unobstructed stretch of ground. Keep both feet on the ground and ensure no block, entity, or wall is immediately ahead.
steps.success_cue: There is enough clear ground ahead for several seconds of uninterrupted forward movement.

steps.action: Perform the first input of the baseline double-tap by pressing and releasing W quickly. Do not press Left Ctrl or any other movement key.
steps.success_cue: W has been released after a brief forward tap, the player remains grounded, and the next step can be performed immediately.

steps.action: Within approximately 200 milliseconds of releasing the first W press, press W again and hold it for about one second. Do not press the separate Sprint control.
steps.exact_input: W (press and hold within approximately 200 ms of the first release)
steps.success_cue: The second W input has been delivered while the player is grounded and has been held for about one second.

steps.action: Release W and wait until all forward movement has stopped. Continue waiting for at least one second so the first double-tap sequence cannot combine with later movement input.
steps.success_cue: No movement key is held and the player is stationary on the ground.

steps.action: Pause the game and navigate back to the controls screen.
steps.success_cue: The Controls screen is open.

steps.action: Locate the Forward entry, which should currently display W, and click its key-binding button so it waits for a replacement input.
steps.exact_input: Click the W button beside Forward
steps.success_cue: The Forward binding is selected and waiting for a new key input.

steps.action: Press G once to assign G to Forward.
steps.success_cue: The Forward entry now displays G.

steps.action: Verify that the Forward entry still displays G and that the controls screen does not indicate a duplicate binding for G. Do not change the separately configured Sprint binding.
steps.success_cue: Forward is uniquely bound to G, and the separate Sprint control remains on a different key.

steps.action: Select Done to leave Controls, select Done to leave Options, and resume the world from the pause menu.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the world and player movement accepts keyboard input.

steps.action: Release all movement keys and wait at least one second. Confirm that the player is grounded, not flying, stationary, and still facing an unobstructed stretch of level ground.
steps.exact_input: Wait at least 1 second with no movement input
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on the ground, no movement key is held, and the route ahead is clear.

steps.action: Perform the first input of the post-rebinding double-tap by pressing and releasing G quickly. Do not press W, Left Ctrl, or any other movement key.
steps.success_cue: G has been released after a brief forward tap, the player remains grounded, and the next step can be performed immediately.

steps.action: Within approximately 200 milliseconds of releasing the first G press, press G again and keep it held. Do not press the separate Sprint control. Hand control to the observation subsystem while G remains held.
steps.exact_input: G (press and hold within approximately 200 ms of the first release)
steps.success_cue: The second G input has just been delivered and remains held while the grounded player has clear terrain ahead.

stor.handoff_condition: Forward is bound to G, the player is grounded in the unobstructed 1.15.2 world, no separate Sprint input is pressed, and the second G press of the quick double-tap has just begun and remains held. Begin observation without releasing G.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, terrain type, difficulty, or single-player versus multiplayer. A new single-player Creative Superflat world is selected as the simplest deterministic environment; the report explicitly makes the full-hunger condition conditional, so it is not applicable in Creative mode.

The report describes the required input timing only as a quick double-tap. An interval of approximately 200 milliseconds is a practical implementation choice intended to unambiguously constitute a quick double-tap; it was not specified by the report.

The report refers to the player's usual Forward button rather than requiring W initially. This plan normalizes the initial binding to the default W key before changing it to the report's example unused key, G.

The report does not explicitly require a clean profile or unmodified client. Those conditions are used to prevent an existing G binding, modified sprint behavior, or retained control configuration from interfering with execution.

source_meta._title: Trapdoors and doors have inconsistent subtitles for being opened and closed

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 23w44a; unmodified client; new single-player Creative-mode world; Update 1.21 experimental features enabled; English (US) language; default resource pack; subtitles enabled; Master Volume and Blocks sound category set above 0%; no nearby redstone components powering the test blocks.
preconditions: Use snapshot 23w44a, the first version listed in the report's Affects versions field. Do not use fix version 25w15a.
Use a new disposable world rather than an existing important world because snapshot and experimental worlds may be unstable.
Use the default resource pack and English (US) if the displayed subtitle wording must be compared directly with the English wording in the report.
Use Creative mode as a deterministic way to obtain the exact Copper Door and Copper Trapdoor without crafting or exploration.
Enable the Update 1.21 experiment during world creation; Copper Doors and Copper Trapdoors are experimental content in snapshot 23w44a.
Keep the test blocks away from levers, redstone torches, pressure plates, buttons, powered blocks, or other redstone sources so that every state change is caused by direct player interaction.
The instructions use default Java Edition controls. If controls have been rebound, use the key assigned to the named action instead.

steps.action: Start Minecraft: Java Edition using an installation configured for snapshot 23w44a. From the title screen, open a new single-player world workflow rather than loading an existing world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open in a client running snapshot 23w44a.

steps.action: Set the world game mode to Creative so the required blocks can be obtained directly from the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Open the experimental-feature configuration from the world-creation screen and enable the experiment named Update 1.21. Accept the experimental-world warning if it appears, then return to the main world-creation screen.
steps.exact_input: More -> Experiments -> Update 1.21: ON -> Done; accept the warning if prompted
steps.success_cue: Update 1.21 is enabled for the new world and the world-creation screen identifies the configuration as experimental.

steps.action: Create the world. Wait without interacting until terrain has rendered, the hotbar is visible, and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the new Creative world, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: If the game is not already using English (US), pause the game, open the language menu, select English (US), and return to the world. This keeps the displayed subtitle wording aligned with the English report.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Language -> English (US) -> Done -> Done
steps.success_cue: Menus and item names are displayed in English.

steps.action: Pause the game and open Music & Sounds. Set Show Subtitles to ON. Also verify that Master Volume and the Blocks sound category are above 0%, then return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Music & Sounds -> Show Subtitles: ON; Master Volume: above 0%; Blocks: above 0% -> Done -> Done
steps.success_cue: The game has resumed with Show Subtitles set to ON and block sound events not muted.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory and select the Search Items tab, identified by the magnifying-glass icon.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory search field and searchable item grid are visible.

steps.action: Search for the door item. Among any oxidation or waxed variants, locate the item whose tooltip is exactly Copper Door, then place one Copper Door into hotbar slot 1.
steps.exact_input: Search: copper door; move the item named exactly "Copper Door" to hotbar slot 1
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains the base, unoxidized item named Copper Door rather than an exposed, weathered, oxidized, or waxed variant.

steps.action: Replace the search text with the trapdoor query. Locate the item whose tooltip is exactly Copper Trapdoor, then place one Copper Trapdoor into hotbar slot 2.
steps.exact_input: Search: copper trapdoor; move the item named exactly "Copper Trapdoor" to hotbar slot 2
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 2 contains the base, unoxidized item named Copper Trapdoor.

steps.action: Close the inventory and move to a clear patch of solid ground with enough empty space above it for a two-block-tall door. Ensure there are no nearby redstone sources that could operate either block.
steps.exact_input: E; use W/A/S/D to move and the mouse to look
steps.success_cue: A clear solid placement area is available, with at least two vertical blocks of empty space and no nearby redstone components.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 1 containing the Copper Door. Aim at the top face of the chosen ground block and use the Place Block action once to place the door.
steps.exact_input: 1 -> right-click the top face of a solid ground block
steps.success_cue: A closed, two-block-tall base Copper Door is standing on the ground.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 2 containing the Copper Trapdoor. Aim at the top face of a nearby ground block and use the Place Block action once. Leave enough space for the trapdoor to rotate open.
steps.exact_input: 2 -> right-click the top face of a nearby solid ground block
steps.success_cue: A closed, horizontal base Copper Trapdoor is placed near the Copper Door and has unobstructed space to open.

steps.action: Stand close enough to interact with both blocks and orient the camera so the Copper Door, Copper Trapdoor, and lower-right subtitle area can be monitored without moving far. Avoid standing on the trapdoor.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D and the mouse; remain within interaction range of both blocks
steps.success_cue: Both test blocks can be targeted from the player's position, and neither block is receiving redstone power.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so that subsequent right-clicks cannot accidentally place another block. Aim the crosshair at the Copper Door.
steps.exact_input: Select any empty hotbar slot, then aim at the Copper Door
steps.success_cue: The player's hand holds no placeable test block and the crosshair is centered on the Copper Door.

steps.action: Use the door once to change it from closed to open. Keep the lower-right subtitle area unobstructed while the interaction occurs.
steps.success_cue: The Copper Door visibly rotates into its open state and one fresh subtitle event is generated for the interaction.

steps.action: Do not interact with either test block until the subtitle entry generated by the door-opening action has faded. This separates the opening and closing events so their entries do not overlap.
steps.success_cue: The Copper Door remains open and the subtitle entry from the previous interaction is no longer visible.

steps.action: Use the Copper Door once more to change it from open to closed.
steps.success_cue: The Copper Door visibly returns to its closed state and one fresh subtitle event is generated for the interaction.

steps.action: Wait until the subtitle entry generated by the door-closing action has faded before operating the trapdoor.
steps.success_cue: The Copper Door remains closed and the previous subtitle entry is no longer visible.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the Copper Trapdoor while retaining an empty hand.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse until the crosshair is centered on the Copper Trapdoor
steps.success_cue: The Copper Trapdoor is closed, directly targeted, and within interaction range.

steps.action: Use the Copper Trapdoor once to change it from closed to open. Keep the lower-right subtitle area unobstructed.
steps.success_cue: The Copper Trapdoor visibly rotates into its open state and one fresh subtitle event is generated for the interaction.

steps.action: Wait until the subtitle entry generated by the trapdoor-opening action has faded. Do not operate the door or make other avoidable block sounds during this interval.
steps.success_cue: The Copper Trapdoor remains open and the previous subtitle entry is no longer visible.

steps.action: Use the Copper Trapdoor once more to change it from open to closed. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem while the newly generated subtitle entry is still displayed.
steps.success_cue: The Copper Trapdoor has visibly returned to its closed state and a fresh subtitle entry from this final interaction is present in the lower-right subtitle area.

stor.handoff_condition: The base Copper Door has been manually opened and closed once, with its two subtitle events temporally separated, and the base Copper Trapdoor has then been manually opened and has just been manually closed. Subtitles remain enabled, no redstone is powering either block, and the subtitle entry produced by the final Copper Trapdoor interaction should still be onscreen for immediate observation.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, world seed, world type, or server type. A new single-player Creative world is selected only to provide deterministic access to the two required blocks.
The report omits that Copper Doors and Copper Trapdoors belong to the Update 1.21 experiment in snapshot 23w44a. The experiment requirement was externally verified for this historical snapshot.
The report does not state a language. English (US) is selected so the autonomous observer can compare the visible text with the English subtitle names given in the report.

The description discusses iron trapdoors as well, but the formal Steps to Reproduce explicitly instruct testing a Copper Door and Copper Trapdoor. This plan therefore does not add an Iron Door or Iron Trapdoor test.
The report does not request oxidation-level or waxed-variant testing. This plan uses only the exact base items named Copper Door and Copper Trapdoor.

Several later affected versions make the copper blocks available without the Update 1.21 experiment, but recommended_version is the first listed affected version, 23w44a, where the experiment must be enabled.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 15w44b in a local single-player Creative-mode world, using keyboard and mouse. Subtitles must be enabled, and the Master Volume and Jukebox/Note Blocks volume controls must be above 0%. No dedicated server, additional players, commands, seed, or coordinates are required.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition snapshot 15w44b rather than the fixed snapshot 20w14a or a modern release.
Allow the launcher to finish downloading the snapshot's standard assets before beginning the test.
Use the standard game resources without a resource pack that replaces music, sound events, subtitle definitions, or language files.
Make sure the game window is large enough for the subtitle display on the lower-right side of the HUD to be visible.
Make sure the operating system has an available audio output device so record playback can be distinguished from a failed jukebox interaction.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Java Edition snapshot 15w44b and start the game. Do not substitute 15w44a, 15w45a, or the fixed snapshot 20w14a.
steps.success_cue: The main-menu version text identifies the running game as Minecraft 15w44b.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Singleplayer, select Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and create the world. The world name and seed may remain at their defaults.
steps.success_cue: The player enters a newly created world and has the Creative-mode HUD, including no health or hunger bars.

steps.action: Wait before configuring the test until the nearby terrain has rendered and inventory and movement input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby blocks are visible, the player can turn and move without world-loading pauses, and the Creative inventory opens when E is pressed.

steps.action: Press Esc, select Options, select Music & Sounds, and click the Show Subtitles control until it reads ON. Return to the game without disabling this option.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Music & Sounds -> Show Subtitles: ON
steps.success_cue: The Show Subtitles control visibly reads ON before the options menus are closed.

steps.action: While still in Music & Sounds, make sure Master Volume and the Jukebox/Note Blocks volume category are both above 0%; a clearly audible setting such as 100% is preferred. Then select Done until gameplay resumes.
steps.success_cue: Gameplay has resumed, subtitles remain enabled, and neither relevant volume control is muted.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Open the Search Items tab, click its search field, enter "Jukebox", and move one Jukebox item into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A Jukebox item is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Clear the Creative inventory search field, enter "Music Disc", and locate the disc whose tooltip identifies the track as C418 - 13. Move that disc into a different empty hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains both a Jukebox and the music disc for track 13 in separate slots.

steps.action: Press E to close the inventory. Select the hotbar slot containing the Jukebox by pressing its corresponding number key or scrolling the mouse wheel. Aim at the top face of a nearby solid ground block and right-click once to place the Jukebox.
steps.success_cue: A Jukebox block is placed on the ground within the player's interaction range.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the C418 - 13 music disc. Keep the crosshair centered on the placed Jukebox and verify that no other menu covers the HUD.
steps.success_cue: The music disc is visible in the player's hand, the Jukebox is under the crosshair, and the normal HUD including the subtitle area is visible.

steps.action: Right-click the placed Jukebox once with the C418 - 13 music disc to insert the disc and start its record sound. Do not click the Jukebox again, because a second interaction can eject the disc. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The Jukebox accepts the disc and record playback begins; the disc is no longer shown in the player's hand as an available hotbar item.

stor.handoff_condition: The C418 - 13 music disc has just been inserted into the placed Jukebox in Minecraft 15w44b while Show Subtitles remains ON and the subtitle HUD is unobstructed. Begin observing the subtitle area immediately without ejecting the disc or triggering additional sounds.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal setup or Steps to Reproduce section and combines many unrelated missing-subtitle sound events accumulated across multiple versions.

Many sounds in the current description were added after the recommended first affected version, Minecraft 15w44b. Therefore, this plan uses the explicitly listed record sound record.13 rather than a later sound such as a 1.9 player attack sound.

The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, or server environment. A local Creative-mode world is selected as the simplest deterministic way to obtain a Jukebox and music disc without introducing crafting or exploration.
This procedure reproduces one representative sound from the report's affected list. It does not attempt to trigger every sound listed in the description and comments.
The report notes that background music and records may have been intentionally unsubtitled, but that question concerns issue evaluation and does not change the execution path requested here.
